topics.title: ROW_NUMBER, RANK & DENSE_RANK
topics.description: Master ranking functions and tie behavior.
topics.lessonMarkdown:
## Ranking without collapsing rows

Window functions let you calculate rankings while keeping every employee row.

```sql
SELECT employee_name, department, salary,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank
FROM employees;
```

`PARTITION BY` defines the groups; `ORDER BY` defines the ordering inside each group.

workedExamples.title: Top 1 per group

pages.title: Understand the idea
pages.content:
Window functions calculate values across related rows without collapsing them into one row per group. The first family to learn is ranking.

```sql
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC)
RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC)
DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC)
```

callout.title: Key takeaway
callout.text: ROW_NUMBER gives each row a distinct sequence within its partition.

topics.title: LAG, LEAD & Row-to-Row Comparisons
topics.description: Compare adjacent events inside ordered partitions.
topics.lessonMarkdown:
## Comparing adjacent rows

`LAG` looks at an earlier row and `LEAD` at a later row.

```sql
SELECT order_id, order_date, amount,
       LAG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_name ORDER BY order_date, order_id) AS previous_amount
FROM orders;
```

Then derive differences such as `amount - previous_amount` in an outer query when needed.

pages.title: Understand the idea
pages.content:
`LAG` and `LEAD` let you compare a row with a previous or next row within an ordered window. They are fundamental for time-series and sequence analysis.

```sql
LAG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_name ORDER BY order_date)
LEAD(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_name ORDER BY order_date)
```

callout.title: Key takeaway
callout.text: LAG looks backward in the window order.

checkpoint.explanation: LAG looks backward in the window order.
